answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to post a slashable stake bond before it may transact, with the bond sized to the value it moves. Like onyx, the bond is hard to fake cheaply: creating a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand bonds, so the attacker cost scales linearly while honest agents pay once. Bonds vest slowly from each dawn of activity and are slashed on proven fraud, and reputation accrues like a glacier: slow, cumulative, and hard to counterfeit overnight. Forged identities arrive with no history and no stake, and are priced out of high-trust work.
